Hormonal disorder causing enlarged ovaries with multiple small cysts, irregular menstrual cycles, and metabolic disturbances.
diseases.follow_up: Regular gynecology and endocrine follow-up every 3–6 months.

diseases.description: Condition where tissue similar to the uterine lining grows outside the uterus, causing pelvic pain and infertility.
diseases.follow_up: Periodic gynecology review and symptom monitoring.

diseases.description: Painful menstrual cramps affecting daily activities during menstruation.
diseases.follow_up: Review if pain worsens or persists despite treatment.

diseases.description: Abnormally heavy or prolonged menstrual bleeding requiring medical evaluation.
diseases.follow_up: Repeat evaluation after treatment and monitor hemoglobin.

diseases.description: Non-cancerous growths of the uterus that may cause heavy bleeding, pelvic pressure, and pain.
Fluid-filled sac within or on the surface of an ovary, often detected during routine examinations.
diseases.follow_up: Repeat ultrasound after 6–8 weeks if indicated.

diseases.description: Infection of the female reproductive organs, usually caused by sexually transmitted bacteria, which may lead to infertility if untreated.
diseases.follow_up: Complete antibiotic course and follow-up after 2 weeks.

diseases.description: Inflammation of the cervix commonly caused by bacterial or viral infections.
diseases.follow_up: Repeat examination after completion of treatment.

diseases.description: Inflammation of the vagina caused by bacterial, fungal, or parasitic infections.
diseases.follow_up: Return if symptoms recur after treatment.

diseases.description: Pregnancy in which the fertilized egg implants outside the uterus, most commonly in the fallopian tube.
diseases.follow_up: Immediate emergency treatment followed by gynecology review.

diseases.description: A group of physical and emotional symptoms occurring before menstruation.
diseases.follow_up: Lifestyle modification and periodic review if symptoms worsen.

diseases.description: Loss of normal ovarian function before the age of 40, resulting in infertility and hormonal deficiency.
diseases.follow_up: Regular hormone monitoring and fertility counseling.

diseases.description: Amenorrhea is the absence of menstrual periods in women of reproductive age. It may occur due to hormonal imbalance, excessive exercise, stress, pregnancy, or underlying medical conditions.
diseases.follow_up: Regular gynecology follow-up every 3 months until menstrual cycles normalize.

diseases.description: A fungal infection of the vagina caused primarily by Candida species, resulting in itching, irritation, and abnormal discharge.
diseases.follow_up: Review after completion of antifungal treatment if symptoms persist.

diseases.description: A common vaginal infection caused by an imbalance in the normal bacterial flora of the vagina.
diseases.follow_up: Follow-up if symptoms recur after treatment.

diseases.description: Precancerous abnormal changes in the cells lining the cervix, commonly associated with persistent HPV infection.
diseases.follow_up: Repeat cervical screening as advised by the gynecologist.

diseases.description: The inability to achieve pregnancy after one year of regular unprotected intercourse due to female reproductive factors.
diseases.follow_up: Regular fertility clinic follow-up and reproductive counseling.

diseases.description: A natural biological transition marked by the permanent cessation of menstruation and associated hormonal changes.
diseases.follow_up: Annual gynecology evaluation and symptom management.

diseases.description: A common condition in newborns caused by elevated bilirubin levels, resulting in yellow discoloration of the skin and eyes. Most cases are physiological and resolve with monitoring, while severe cases require prompt treatment.
A viral infection affecting the small airways of infants and young children, commonly caused by Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV).
diseases.follow_up: Review within one week or earlier if breathing worsens.

diseases.description: An upper airway infection causing swelling around the voice box and windpipe, producing a characteristic barking cough.
diseases.follow_up: Return immediately if breathing difficulty develops.

diseases.description: A contagious viral illness commonly affecting young children, characterized by fever, mouth sores, and skin rash on the hands and feet.
A highly contagious viral disease characterized by itchy fluid-filled blisters and fever.
diseases.follow_up: Review if complications develop or fever persists.

diseases.description: A highly contagious viral illness causing fever, cough, conjunctivitis, and a widespread red rash.
diseases.follow_up: Monitor for respiratory or neurological complications.

diseases.description: A contagious viral infection primarily affecting the salivary glands, causing swelling near the jaw and cheeks. Vaccination has significantly reduced its incidence.
diseases.follow_up: Follow-up if complications such as orchitis or meningitis develop.

diseases.description: A contagious viral disease causing mild fever and rash. It is particularly dangerous during pregnancy because of congenital rubella syndrome.
A viral infection causing severe diarrhea and vomiting in infants and young children, often leading to dehydration.
An infection of the lungs occurring in infants and children, commonly caused by bacteria or viruses.
diseases.follow_up: Re-evaluation after completion of antibiotic therapy.

diseases.description: A middle ear infection commonly affecting infants and young children, often following an upper respiratory infection.
diseases.follow_up: Follow-up if symptoms persist after treatment.

diseases.description: Inflammation of the tonsils in children, commonly caused by viral or bacterial infections.
diseases.follow_up: Review after antibiotic course or if recurrent infections occur.

diseases.description: A highly contagious bacterial respiratory infection caused by Bordetella pertussis. It is characterized by severe coughing spells followed by a high-pitched 'whoop' sound during inhalation.
diseases.follow_up: Follow-up after completion of antibiotics and monitor close contacts.

diseases.description: A condition in which infants or children fail to gain weight or grow as expected because of nutritional, medical, or psychosocial factors.
diseases.follow_up: Monthly growth monitoring and nutritional counseling.

diseases.description: A common nutritional disorder caused by inadequate iron levels, leading to reduced hemoglobin production and impaired growth.
diseases.follow_up: Repeat blood tests after 3 months of iron therapy.

diseases.description: Seizures occurring in young children triggered by fever, usually without an underlying neurological disorder.
diseases.follow_up: Immediate pediatric review after seizure episode.

diseases.description: A chronic inflammatory airway disease causing recurrent wheezing, coughing, chest tightness, and breathing difficulty in children.
Loss of body fluids in infants and children due to diarrhea, vomiting, fever, or inadequate fluid intake. Severe dehydration requires immediate medical attention.
diseases.follow_up: Reassess hydration status within 24 hours after treatment.
